title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
subtitle: Calculus, linear algebra, probability, optimization and information theory, with machine learning in mind.
preface: This book is the mathematics that the Machine Learning book uses: single and multivariable calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistical estimation, optimization and information theory. It matches the lower-division and early upper-division courses at Stanford (Math 51, CS 109, CS 205L) and Berkeley (Math 53, Math 54, EECS 16A/16B, CS 70, Stat 134, EECS 127).

The treatment is concise. Definitions come with a reason for being, results come with a proof or a derivation when the argument teaches something, and examples are numerical and checked. Where a concept matters for machine learning, the text says where it reappears.

Read the parts in order: Calculus, Linear Algebra, Probability, Estimation, then Optimization and Information. The Linear Algebra and Probability parts are the ones to know best before starting Machine Learning.

parts.title: Calculus
parts.blurb: Derivatives, integrals and series in one variable, then gradients, Jacobians and Hessians in many.

parts.title: Linear Algebra
parts.blurb: Vectors, matrices, subspaces, orthogonality, eigenvalues and the singular value decomposition.

parts.title: Probability
parts.blurb: Events, random variables, joint distributions, the Gaussian and limit theorems.

parts.title: Estimation
parts.blurb: Maximum likelihood, Bayesian estimation and the properties of estimators.

parts.title: Optimization and Information
parts.blurb: Convexity, gradient methods, constrained optimization, duality, entropy and divergence.
